sentences.text:
He has been ordered to undergo life imprisonment with a fine of Rs. 10,000/-
and in default of payment of fine, to further suffer simple imprisonment for a period of ten months for the offence under Section 376(A)(B) of the IPC and to undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year with a fine of Rs. 1,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to further suffer simple imprisonment for one month for the offence under Section 506 of the IPC.
4.
The prosecution case is to the effect that the informant (mother of the victim) gave a written report, stating therein that on 10.08.2020, at around 02:00 P.M., she had sent Patna High Court CR.
APP ( DB) No.146 of 2024(10) dt.07-10-2025 her daughter (victim) to a nearby shop of the village to buy thread
. It is alleged that the victim returned home after an hour and she was crying.

When her mother inquired about the same, the victim narrated that the appellant (Triloki Singh)
intercepted her midway and asked her that the shopkeeper was calling her again and told her that he would give her the wire as demanded by her father.
The victim narrated that the appellant took her to his house and closed the door and when she tried to raise alarm, she was threatened of dire consequences.
It has further been alleged that the accused/appellant opened the pant of the victim and committed wrong with her.
The informant has alleged that she immediately went to the house of the accused/appellant and found the room locked.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that from bare perusal of the judgment of conviction, it would be evident that the learned Trial Court has not taken into account the glaring and pulpable discrepancies in the evidence of the prosecution.

It has been submitted that most importantly, P.W.
2 (victim) in her deposition, during the course of cross- examination, has stated that she had not seen Triloki Singh (appellant) prior to the incident.

She has also stated that prior to this date of occurrence, she did not know the person whose Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.146 of 2024(10)
dt.07-10-2025 name was Triloki Singh (appellant).

It has further been submitted that contrary to the statements made by the victim (P.W. 2), the informant (P.W. 3) in the F.I.R. has stated that the victim came home and disclosed that it was Triloki Singh (appellant), who had stopped her on her way back to home from the shop.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant has further submitted that the Doctor (P.W. 1), who has examined the victim, found no injuries on the buttock, perineum and vulva of the victim.
The hymen was ruptured, but that is not attributed to any sexual act.
It has been submitted that no spermatozoa was found alive or dead in the vaginal swab taken for examination.
P.W. 1, during her cross-examination, has stated that when a girl of 11 to 12 years is subjected to forceful rape, she has to suffer injuries around her private parts.
The Doctor (P.W. 1), during the medical examination, has not found any redness, tenderness, sallowness or painfulness around the vaginal orifice of the victim.
It has further been submitted that as per the seizure-list, the sky-colour half pant of the victim was seized and sent for medical examination.
However, from the F.S.L. report, it would be evident that there was no blood or semen on the exhibit material.

It has, thus, been submitted that Triloki Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19277476/

7. It has been argued by the learned counsel for the appellant that there is material contradiction in the statements of the victim (P.W. 2) as also her mother (P.W. 3).
It has lastly been submitted that the prosecution has not been able to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubts and the appellant is in custody for more than five years by now.

8. While opposing the prayer for suspension of sentence, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 2 as also the learned Addl. Public Prosecutor for the State have submitted that the prosecution, through the evidences, have been able to prove the case against the appellant and looking at the nature of offence, the appellant does not deserve suspension of sentence during pendency of the appeal.
It has been submitted that the victim in her statement, recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. (Exhibit-2), has supported the occurrence and has reiterated the prosecution story as stated in the F.I.R.

It has further been submitted that the medical report of the victim has also given an opinion that sexual act is present, but the Doctor (P.W. 1) has opined that his opinion is given solely for the reason that the hymen was ruptured.
The accused-appellant was Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.146 of 2024(10) dt.07-10-2025 not medically examined.

9. Having regard to the submissions noted hereinabove and the evidences which we have prima facie gone through, we have observed that the victim (P.W. 2) has stated in her evidence that she did not know the appellant prior to the said incident and she had not seen him by face prior to the occurrence.
If it is so, it seems highly difficult to understand as to how she would name the appellant to her mother.
Her mother is the informant of this case and has claimed in her written information that her daughter told her that on way, the appellant met her and asked her to come to the shop.

The FIR itself has been lodged on the basis of the information given by the victim but the victim (P.W. 2)
has stated that the appellant met her at the door of Panditji and she did not know at that time that the person who met her at the door of Panditji was this appellant, in these circumstances, the initial prosecution version that she was returning from shop and on way the appellant met her gets changed and now it is stated that the appellant met her at the door of Panditji.

The I.O. (P.W. 5) has categorically stated that he had not recorded statement of the shopkeeper or any person in the boundary of the place of occurrence and in the whole investigation he had recorded statement of only father and Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.146 of 2024(10) dt.07-10-2025 mother of the victim.
He had not got the accused medically examined.

We have also observed that the medical report of the victim does not support the factum of penetrative sexual act and the informant has drastically changed her statement in course of evidence where she has stated in her examination-in-chief that the accused had committed rape on the victim from the backside/behind,
the victim has stated that she had stayed in the house of the appellant only for one minute.
The Doctor (P.W. 1) has not found any external injuries on face, neck, back and abdomen.
No injuries on buttock, perineum and vulva.

The only thing which is stated is that hymen was ruptured but the Doctor (P.W. 1) has admitted that presence and absence of hymen does not prove or disprove whether someone has engaged in sexual activity.
He also admitted that, in his opinion, he has not stated whether the hymen was newly ruptured or old ruptured.

sentences.text: We have also noticed that the FSL report does not corroborate the factum of penetrative assault on the victim, no blood or semen has been found on the pant of the victim.
The medical report or the FSL report completely rule out a case of penetrative sexual act with the victim, the defence has suggested that it is a case of false implication to misappropriate Rs.
Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB)
No.146 of 2024(10) dt.07-10-2025 1,00,000/-, which the father of the victim had taken from the appellant.

We have noticed admission on the part of P.W. 3 that the appellant was friend of her husband, but her husband (P.W.
4) has stated that the appellant had never come to his house though his house is at a distance of only five minutes from the house of P.W. 4, these are some apparent and palpable observations showing the vacillating stand of the prosecution witnesses, the appellant has already remained in jail for five years but this appeal is of the year 2024 which is not likely to be heard in near future, in such circumstances, we are of the opinion that the appellant would deserve suspension of sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal.

11. Let the sentence of the appellant, named-above, be suspended and he be released on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on his furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Addl. District &
Sessions Judge-VI-cum-Special Judge, POCSO Act, Buxar, in connection with POCSO Case No. 28 of 2020 (C.I.S. No. 28 of 2020), arising out of Buxar (Mahila) P.S. Case No. 70 of 2020.
12.
The fine, if any, imposed as a part of sentence shall remain suspended during pendency of the appeal.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.146 of 2024(10) dt.07-10-2025 13.
It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only prima facie and tentative for the purpose of suspension of sentence and bail only, which would not cause prejudice to either parties.

14. List this appeal for hearing on its turn.
